title: Repricing the shop in one pass
target: How to reprice what you sell in Supermarket Simulator in one deliberate pass instead of shelf by shelf: the bulk panel, the pricing screen's sorting and quick picks, dynamic goods, offers and discounts.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with stock on the shelves
The pricing side of the shop reachable
A rough idea of the margin you want

steps.do: Reprice in bulk rather than shelf by shelf, because prices can be set in bulk through a panel of its own.
steps.because: prices can be set in bulk through a dedicated manager and panel (BulkPricingManager, BulkPricingPanel)

steps.do: Know which section of the bulk panel you are working in, because the panel is built from typed sections.
steps.because: the bulk pricing panel is built from typed sections (BulkPricingSection, BulkPricingSectionType)

steps.do: Sort the list before you start changing anything, because the screen has its own sorting button, kinds and state.
steps.because: the list can be sorted with its own button, kinds and state (PricingSortingButton, PricingSortingType, PricingSortingState)

steps.do: Use the quick picks for prices you set again and again, because there are quick-pick buttons with a group, a mode and their own data.
steps.because: a price can be picked quickly through quick-pick buttons and their data (PriceQuickPickButton, PriceQuickPickGroup, PriceQuickPickMode, PriceQuickPickSO)

steps.do: Open the pricing canvas from the pricing side of the shop rather than hunting a menu, because that is how the game reaches it.
steps.because: prices are set on a canvas of their own, opened by its own interaction, on the pricing side of the shop (SettingPriceCanvas, PricingInteraction, Pricing)

steps.do: Expect some goods to price themselves, because there is a kind of product whose price is dynamic.
steps.because: there is a kind of product whose price is dynamic (DynamicPriceProduct)

steps.do: Let the game evaluate the prices rather than trusting what you typed, because evaluation is its own step and a change raises a notification.
steps.because: prices are evaluated by a manager of their own and a change raises a notification (PriceEvaluationManager, PriceChangeNotification)

steps.do: Check the margin rather than only the number, because margins are worked out through their own calculation.
steps.because: margins are computed through a calculation of their own (ComputeRequiredMarginsDelegate)

steps.do: Treat a wholesale offer as a separate decision from a price, because offers have a manager, a kind, a time limit and a canvas.
steps.because: wholesale offers run through a manager and settings of their own, with a kind, a time limit and a canvas (WholeSaleManager, WholeSaleSettingsSO, OfferType, offertime, WholeSaleOfferCanvas)

steps.do: Keep discounts apart from prices, because they are a system of their own with their own panel and rate.
steps.because: discounts are a separate system with a panel and a rate of their own (DiscountManager, DiscountPanel, discountRate)

commonMistakes: Walking the aisles changing tags one at a time when the bulk panel exists for exactly that.
Repricing before sorting and losing track of which goods have already been changed.
Setting a number that looks right on a tag without looking at the margin.
Treating a wholesale offer or a discount as if it were a price change.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
